title: Integer musical time: ticks, tempo maps, samples

recipes.name: Compute tick-to-microseconds with u128 intermediate and floor
recipes.what: SMF stores tempo as u24 microseconds-per-quarter and tick deltas as u28; the law evaluates the exact rational tick×tempo÷PPQ in u128 and floors once per segment.
recipes.how: Inside an extern "C" function, write `let us = ((tick as u128 * tempo as u128) / ppq as u128) as u64;`. The single integer division is the floor.
recipes.gotchas: Dividing before multiplying truncates early and loses tempo resolution; u64 intermediates overflow at max tick × max tempo.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the likely second integer timeline in samples: the wasm cdylib must convert ticks to exact microseconds without floating point.

checks.label: tick to microseconds via u128 on wasm

recipes.name: Compute tick-to-samples through tempo map with u128
recipes.what: Samples are derived from ticks by the exact rational tick×tempo×sample_rate÷(PPQ×1_000_000), computed in u128 and floored once.
recipes.how: Compute `let num = tick as u128 * tempo as u128 * sample_rate as u128; let den = ppq as u128 * 1_000_000u128; let samples = (num / den) as u64;` inside the exported function.
recipes.gotchas: Reordering to divide early introduces rounding errors; the full numerator must stay in u128 until the final division.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the likely separately pinned renderer: sample positions must be exact integers computed from the tempo map inside the wasm law.

checks.label: tick to samples via u128 on wasm

recipes.name: Choose PPQ divisible by 3 and 5 for exact tuplets
recipes.what: PPQ values 480, 960 and 3840 are divisible by 3 and 5, yielding exact integer tick deltas for triplets and quintuplets, but not for septuplets.
recipes.how: Select a PPQ that is a multiple of the desired tuplet ratio; verify exactness with `ppq % ratio == 0`.
recipes.gotchas: 3840 is not divisible by 7, so a septuplet grid must be approximated or handled by a higher-level tuplet track.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the fixed PPQ lock item: the chosen PPQ must be high enough and factorable so that common tuplets are exact integers.

checks.label: PPQ divisibility for tuplets

recipes.name: Calculate bar and beat from tick under SMF time signatures
recipes.what: SMF FF 58 stores numerator and a power-of-two denominator; bar/beat arithmetic uses ticks_per_beat = PPQ × 4 ÷ 2^denom and ticks_per_bar = ticks_per_beat × num.
recipes.how: Parse the four TimeSignature bytes; compute `beat_unit = 1u32 << denom_exp; ticks_per_beat = (ppq * 4) / beat_unit;` then derive bar, beat and tick-in-beat with `/` and `%`.
recipes.gotchas: The denominator byte is the exponent, not the written denominator; e.g., 4/4 uses denom_exp = 2.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the integer tick timeline: the law must locate events in bars and beats for display and looping without floating point.

checks.label: bar beat from tick under 4-4 time

recipes.name: Refuse on overflow with checked arithmetic
recipes.what: The law uses checked_mul and checked_add so that any overflow in time calculations returns a refusal instead of wrapping or panicking.
recipes.how: Chain `tick.checked_mul(tempo)?.checked_add(carry)?` and propagate None as a refusal event to the host.
recipes.gotchas: Unchecked `*` panics in debug and wraps in release by default; strict_mul always panics, which is unsuitable for a law that must refuse gracefully.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on deterministic replay: an overflow must produce a defined refusal in the action log, not a wrap or trap.

checks.label: checked_mul returns None on overflow

recipes.name: Enable overflow-checks in release or rely on checked ops
recipes.what: Inference: The release profile disables overflow-checks by default, so unchecked operators wrap; the law should either set overflow-checks = true or use exclusively checked methods.
recipes.how: Add `overflow-checks = true` under `[profile.release]` in Cargo.toml, or prefer `checked_` methods explicitly.
recipes.gotchas: Relying on the default release profile makes `+` and `*` silently wrap, corrupting musical position.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the deterministic replay and hash: silent wrap in release would desynchronise the score from the action log.

recipes.name: Reserve Wrapping arithmetic for hash state only
recipes.what: Wrapping<u64> provides modular arithmetic for hashing and checksums, but must never be used for tick or sample counts because it silently wraps on underflow.
recipes.how: Use `Wrapping(hash)` for the state hash; use `checked_add` or exact integer ops for the timeline.
recipes.gotchas: Accidentally using Wrapping for deltas makes `zero - one` jump to u32::MAX, destroying bar/beat alignment.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the state hash: the law hashes its state with wrapping arithmetic, but the musical timeline must never wrap.

checks.label: Wrapping sub wraps around

recipes.name: Use u128 intermediates on wasm32-unknown-unknown
recipes.what: u128 compiles and runs on wasm32-unknown-unknown via compiler-builtins, so the law can safely use u128 for tempo-map intermediates.
recipes.how: Cast operands to u128 inside the wasm-exported function; the compiler lowers the math to wasm i64/i32 operations.
recipes.gotchas: u128 is not in the wasm C ABI, so extern "C" functions must not pass or return u128 directly; use u64 and reconstruct internally.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the wasm32-unknown-unknown cdylib target: u128 is available in core for exact integer time math.

checks.label: u128 math compiles and runs on wasm32

recipes.name: Exclude f64 seconds from the law time path
recipes.what: f64 cannot represent every u64 value exactly, so microseconds and samples are kept as integers; midly’s second_f32 exists only for SMPTE display.
recipes.how: Store tempo as u24 microseconds-per-quarter and onsets as u64 ticks or samples; never convert through `as f64`.
recipes.gotchas: A single `tick as f64 * tempo as f64 / ppq as f64` introduces rounding that shifts note onsets by whole samples.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the no-floating-point rule: the law’s state and time path must contain no f64 values.

checks.label: f64 loses precision for large u64

recipes.name: Carry division remainders across tempo segments
recipes.what: Floor division is not associative across segment sums: floor(a/c)+floor(b/c) can be less than floor((a+b)/c); the law carries remainders to keep cumulative time exact.
recipes.how: For each segment compute `quot = tick * tempo / PPQ` and `rem = (tick * tempo) % PPQ`; add `rem` to the next segment’s numerator before division.
recipes.gotchas: Flooring each segment independently drops fractional ticks that accumulate into audible micro-timing drift across tempo changes.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the integer tempo map: crossing a tempo boundary must not lose fractional ticks between the score and the sample timeline.

checks.label: floor division remainder carry fixes drift
